prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Scope: hospital automated medication dispensing/returns: order intake, pharmacy prep/verification, cold storage, tube transport, ward cabinets, returns. Aliases: Morrowglass=Medication Order Gateway; Cinderwake=Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot; Juniper=Pharmacy Verification Station; Bluejay=Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler; Tallowmere=Medication Return Kiosk; Copperfield=Pharmacy Technician; Larkspur=Registered Nurse; Stonewake=Biomedical Engineer. Elements: - Medication Order Gateway: validates patient/product/dose/route/timing; rejects incomplete with reason; routes to pharmacy; order status; Order Reconciliation Snapshot. - Pharmacy Verification Station: final controlled checkpoint; order vs scanned product; mismatch holds until authorized resolution; records approver, time, med IDs; Dose Exception Review Slip, Batch Release Note (to South Ward Cabinet Controller), audit record. - Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot: only active authorized orders; inhibited until pharmacy authorization; uses Snapshot; exception stops/holds/preserves scans; Priority Refill Tote Tag. - Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler: per-compartment timestamped temperature vs limits; calibrated probes; lot/expiry tracing; excursion/probe loss makes stock ineligible; uses Cold Chain Handoff Card; access/door logs; offline alarms persist. - Pneumatic Tube Network: compliant loads; reports segment status, transfer progress, delivery confirmation to console. - East Tube Dispatch Console: keeps approved route map, segment availability; checks route vs destination, availability, approved config version (not operator segments); checks conflicts/interlocks; stale/incomplete status holds capsule for operator review; lost sensor comms = segment unavailable; logs transit interruption (capsule ID, last location, time); alerts Pharmacy Technician on stalled/unconfirmed transfer; after recovery needs refreshed status + approved route; Tube Route Exception Ticket. West console exists. Route/temperature records keep timestamps, equipment IDs. - North/South Ward Cabinet Controllers: availability, arrivals; versioned approved configuration before enabling compartments (no config blocks routine dispensing); min/max; role auth; high-risk extra confirmation; rejects mismatch. North uses Priority Refill Tote Tag; South reports failed lock/access. - Medication Return Kiosk: Return Bin Audit Label. Actors: - Clinical Pharmacist: verifies order vs product/strength/form/dose/route/time, patient IDs/label; resolves unclear orders via Gateway; exceptions, excursion disposition; high-risk independent second check recorded. - Pharmacy Technician: prep; checks package integrity/lot/expiry; Cold Chain Handoff Card; reconciliation queue

Document units:
S205: The South Ward Cabinet Controller checks its local compartment mapping, access rules, and supported medication classes against that configuration.
S206: The cabinet reports Ready for Dispense only after its configuration checks and required device self-tests pass.
S207: The Registered Nurse authenticates at the cabinet and selects the medication associated with the active patient order.
S208: The South Ward Cabinet Controller checks the requested selection against its local authorization rules before unlocking a compartment.
S209: The cabinet records the user, order reference, compartment access, and transaction time for audit review.
S210: Stonewake reviews the received operational record, correlates its equipment identifiers and timestamps with local telemetry, and records an engineering disposition.
S211: The Biomedical Engineer uses the exception ticket to identify the affected path and compare reported symptoms with equipment telemetry.
S212: The Biomedical Engineer checks whether the reported condition is isolated to one device or indicates a broader service risk.
S213: When a hardware or control fault is suspected, the affected equipment is placed in Out of Service status.
S214: The Biomedical Engineer isolates the affected subsystem and performs only the diagnostic steps approved for that equipment.
S215: The IT Operations Specialist investigates authentication, interface, and time-synchronization faults that could affect transaction records.
S216: The Medication Safety Officer reviews any discrepancy that could change medication identity, access control, or patient risk.
S217: The Clinical Pharmacist keeps affected medication unavailable until the relevant order and product checks are repeated successfully.
S218: The Biomedical Engineer records the corrective action, test evidence, and approvals required to return the equipment to operation.
S219: Equipment remains Out of Service until required functional checks pass and the responsible staff approve its return.
S220: Audit records retain timestamps, equipment identifiers, and disposition details to support operational review and investigation.
S221: A cabinet outage is treated as a service incident when the cabinet stops responding, reports a fault, or fails a dispensing check.
S222: The IT Operations Specialist uses the Cabinet Downtime Notice to open a controlled incident record and identify the affected cabinet.
S223: The IT Operations Specialist checks controller status, network connectivity, and recent event logs before attempting recovery.
S224: The IT Operations Specialist records the time the fault was detected and the affected equipment identifier.
S225: The affected North Ward Cabinet Controller or South Ward Cabinet Controller remains Out of Service while the cause is assessed.
S226: The IT Operations Specialist isolates the fault where necessary to prevent repeated dispense requests from reaching an unavailable cabinet.
